newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - HA-LO sees Q3, year net up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - HA-LO sees Q3, year net up.

text.p: The founder and chairman of HA-LO Industries Inc said Monday the company is generating double digit revenue growth and expects to report higher 1996 third quarter and year-end earnings.

1996 year pre-tax income for HA-LO, which produces hundreds of promotional products carrying brands, logos or advertising messages, is estimated by analysts at $17 million, up from the $4.98 million earned in the 1995 year.
"We're comfortable with those numbers," said Lou Weisbach, HA-LO founder and chairman, in an interview.
The 1996 year estimate translates to per share earnings of $0.67 a share based on about 14 million shares outstanding. "We're comfortable with estimates of $0.67 a share," he said.
In 1995, the Niles, Ill.-based company reported earnings of $0.51 on 5.8 million shares outstanding. Sales totaled $172.9 million including contributions from acquisitions.
For the third quarter, analysts estimate earnings of $0.16 on the larger number of shares outstanding. HA-LO expects to report results during the first week of November.
"We are certainly comfortable there on the higher number of shares," Weisbach said.
In the 1995 third quarter, the company earned $0.20 a share on sales of $48 million including acquisitions.

Third quarter results benefited from strong internal growth as well as from acquisitions and strategic alliances, all factors which are expected to continue into the fourth quarter and beyond, he said.
"We expect to continue to have internal growth between 25 and 35 percent year after year," Weisbach said.
HA-LO has said its goal is to generate sales of $1 billion by the year 2000.

The goal is "very achievable and we believe we can do it, but certain things have to fall into place from an acquisition perspective," Weisbach said. However, he added, "We don't feel pressured to reach that goal just to make deals."
In recent months, HA-LO has added to its alliances with Mail Boxes Etc, Sharper Image and PACE Entertainment Corp.

In early 1995, an alliance was formed with Montgomery Ward, the largest privately held U.S. retailer, to provide premiums to get shoppers into stores and help drive the retailer's credit card business. This alliance generated sales of about $29 million and estimates are for $35 million in 1996. Year to date, sales from the alliance have already reached $34 million, Weisbach said.
Weisbach expects the alliance to continue to contribute to its results, although Montgomery Ward said last week it was looking for a new chief executive.

"We certainly think it will be steady, but it will depend on management and what their objectives are," he said. He said he expects the new management to be promotionally aggressive and "that would be a benefit for us if that would happen."
HA-LO shares were up 1/2 at 30-1/4 Monday.
